issues.name: Migratekit: fix README + track ClickHouse migrations in Postgres
issues.description:
We want to (1) update the README because it no longer matches the current code/API, and (2) change ClickHouse migration tracking/locking to use Postgres `public.migrations` + Postgres advisory locks instead of ClickHouse `migrations` + `migration_locks`.

Why:
- ClickHouse is awkward for authoritative state (migration ledgers + locks) because it’s eventually-consistent (ReplacingMergeTree) and restore/merge semantics are part-based, not row-upsert.
- Postgres already has a correct ledger table (`public.migrations`) with a `database` column and uniqueness `(app, database, name)`. We can reuse it for ClickHouse by writing rows with `database='clickhouse'`.
tasks: === README ===

[x] Update README examples to match current APIs:
  - Postgres: `NewPostgres(db, app)` and `.WithSchema(schema)`
  - ClickHouse: `NewClickHouse(&ClickHouseConfig{...})`

[x] Update README to reflect current Postgres locking:
  - Postgres uses advisory locks (no `public.migration_locks` table)
  - Postgres tracking table is `public.migrations` with `database='postgres'`
[x] Document new behavior: ClickHouse migrations are tracked in Postgres with `database='clickhouse'`.
=== CLICKHOUSE TRACKING IN POSTGRES ===

[x] Add a Postgres-backed tracker/locker helper:
  - Create/ensure `public.migrations` exists (same schema as today)
  - List applied by `(app, database)`
  - Record applied via INSERT/ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
  - Acquire/release an advisory lock dedicated to ClickHouse migrations (separate from Postgres migrations lock key).

[x] Refactor ClickHouse migrator to use the Postgres tracker:
  - `Applied()` reads from Postgres `public.migrations` where `database='clickhouse'`
  - `Apply()` records into Postgres after successful ClickHouse migration execution
  - `Lock()`/`Unlock()` use Postgres advisory locks (no ClickHouse `migration_locks`).

[x] Deprecate ClickHouse tables `migrations` / `migration_locks`:
  - Stop creating them in `ClickHouse.Setup()` when Postgres tracking is enabled (legacy tables used only for fallback)
  - Do not auto-drop (leave cleanup to operators)
  - Update docs to reflect deprecation.

[x] Add fallback behavior:
  - Default/preferred: Postgres-backed tracker for ClickHouse migrations when a Postgres connection is provided.
  - Fallback: if Postgres is not provided or is unavailable, use the legacy ClickHouse `migrations` + `migration_locks` tables.
  - Document the behavior clearly and make it explicit in the ClickHouse constructor/config (no silent partial tracking).
=== TESTS ===

[x] Add/extend tests for:
  - Recording ClickHouse applied migrations into Postgres (`database='clickhouse'`).
  - Locking uses Postgres advisory locks when PostgresDB is configured.
  - Backward-compat story: PostgresDB absent continues to use legacy ClickHouse tracking (covered implicitly by not removing legacy code paths).
=== HOST APP INTEGRATION NOTES ===

[x] Document required inputs for running ClickHouse migrations:
  - ClickHouse connection config
  - Postgres connection for tracking/locking
  - What to do during restores (e.g. always clear/truncate any legacy `migration_locks` if it exists).

issues.name: Migratekit cleanup: simplify ClickHouse + consolidate Postgres tracker
issues.description:
Now that ClickHouse migrations are tracked+locked in Postgres only (no ClickHouse tracker tables), we can simplify migratekit:

Targets:
- Remove legacy/low-value fields/options.
- Delete dead code from old ClickHouse lock-table era.
- Consolidate duplicate Postgres tracking-table setup logic.
- Keep the public API minimal and the README accurate.
tasks: [x] Remove `ClickHouseConfig.LockID` and all usage (lock key derives from ClientAddr+Database+Cluster).
[x] Delete any remaining ClickHouse lock-table remnants (TTL/expiry helpers, lock SQL, constants used only by legacy `migration_locks`).
[x] Consolidate Postgres `public.migrations` DDL into one shared helper used by both `postgres.go` and `tracker_postgres.go` (avoid duplication).

[x] Tighten ClickHouse migrator:
  - `Setup()` only ensures Postgres tracker is ready
  - remove any leftover mode/fallback scaffolding
  - ensure lock key is stable and scoped to cluster/db appropriately

[x] README cleanup:
  - ensure there is no mention of ClickHouse fallback tables
  - ensure examples match final APIs after this cleanup
[x] Verify: `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...`

issues.name: Migratekit hardening: fix advisory-lock pooling bug, ordering, and latent footguns
issues.description:
Findings from a 2026-06-10 code review (driven by authkit's sqlc transition adopting migratekit as its only migration runner). Two real bugs and several latent footguns, ranked by severity.

BUG 1 — ADVISORY LOCK DOESN'T ACTUALLY LOCK (most important): Postgres.Lock()/Unlock() and postgresTracker.Lock()/Unlock() run pg_advisory_lock/pg_advisory_unlock via db.ExecContext on a *sql.DB POOL. Session advisory locks are bound to the CONNECTION that took them, but every subsequent ExecContext (the migrations themselves, and Unlock) may run on a DIFFERENT pooled connection. Mutual exclusion between replicas is therefore only accidental (works when the pool serially reuses one idle conn — why it has worked so far). Worse: Unlock on the wrong connection returns 'advisory lock was not held', the deferred call discards that error, and the REAL lock stays held on the original pooled connection until it is recycled — other replicas then block in Lock() indefinitely.

BUG 2 — LEXICAL SORT BREAKS AT MIGRATION 10 FOR UNPADDED NAMES: LoadFromFS sorts by raw filename, but Prefix() explicitly supports unpadded names like '1-create-users.up.sql'. Lexically '10_x' < '2_x', so migrations 10+ apply BEFORE 2-9 if names are not zero-padded. Works today only because every consumer zero-pads.

FOOTGUNS: (3) tracking by normalized Prefix() silently swallows collisions — two files sharing a numeric prefix ('002_users' + '002_roles', or '0042_x' vs '42_y') means the second is treated as applied and silently skipped, with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING hiding any trace; (4) missing-table detection via strings.Contains(err, 'does not exist') breaks under non-English lc_messages — should check SQLSTATE 42P01; (5) substituteTemplates silently injects EMPTY STRINGS for unset env vars (a typo'd {{CLICKHOUSE_PASWORD}} ships an empty password) and rewrites matches inside SQL string literals, unconditionally, for Postgres too; (6) splitSQL (ClickHouse path) is not quote-aware — a literal ';' or '--' inside a string corrupts the statement split; (7) Postgres.Close() closes the caller's *sql.DB, which the migrator does not own; (8) ClickHouse partial-apply semantics (no transactions; failure at statement 3/5 leaves 1-2 applied and unrecorded, rerun re-executes them) are undocumented.

NON-GOALS: sqlc adoption — deliberately rejected. migratekit's ~6 bookkeeping queries target a table whose creation is migratekit's own job (chicken-and-egg with sqlc's schema input), and dynamic bits (search_path, advisory locks) are exactly the raw-SQL escape hatch. No bun anywhere in this module — nothing to remove. Optional, only if go.sum weight ever bothers consumers: split ClickHouse support into a migratekit/clickhouse submodule so Postgres-only consumers (e.g. authkit) stop pulling clickhouse-go transitively.
tasks: === BUG FIXES ===

[x] Pin the advisory lock to a single connection. Done 2026-06-10: Postgres.Lock acquires a dedicated *sql.Conn (db.Conn) and stores it on the migrator; Unlock releases the lock on that same pinned conn then closes it (closing is the safety net that frees the session lock even if pg_advisory_unlock fails); guarded by a mutex with explicit double-lock/double-unlock errors. Same treatment for postgresTracker.Lock/Unlock (ClickHouse path), including an unlock-key mismatch check.

[x] Unlock robustness. Done 2026-06-10: Unlock runs under context.WithoutCancel so a cancelled migration still releases the lock (covered by an explicit test); ApplyMigrations no longer discards the deferred Unlock error — it is errors.Join'ed into the returned error.

[x] Fix migration ordering. Done 2026-06-10: LoadFromFS sorts by numeric prefix (1, 2, 9, 10, 100), tie-breaking and non-numeric names lexically; regression test TestLoadFromFS_NumericOrder covers the 2-vs-10 case, TestLoadFromFS_ZeroPaddedOrderUnchanged pins existing behavior.
=== FAIL-FAST GUARDS ===

[x] Duplicate-prefix detection. Done 2026-06-10: LoadFromFS errors when two .up.sql files normalize to the same Prefix(), naming both files; tests cover 002_users+002_roles and 0042_x+42_y. Verified no existing consumer migration dir (openrails, doujins, authkit) trips it.

[x] SQLSTATE check. Done 2026-06-10: took BOTH halves of the either/or — ApplyMigrations now always runs Setup() first (one retry for Postgres's concurrent CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS race), deleting the entire duplicated missing-table branch; ValidateAllApplied (which must stay read-only) detects undefined_table via errors.As to interface{ SQLState() string } == 42P01 (works for lib/pq and pgx), with the old substring check kept only as a fallback for drivers without SQLState.

[x] Template substitution safety. Done 2026-06-10: substituteTemplates returns an error naming the variable when a referenced env var is UNSET (os.LookupEnv); explicitly-empty vars still substitute (intentional); ON_CLUSTER passthrough preserved. Decision on opt-in: substitution stays enabled for both engines — making it opt-in would break existing ClickHouse migrations, and the unset-var error removes the actual footgun. Documented in README.
=== POLISH ===

[x] splitSQL quote-awareness. Done 2026-06-10: rewrote as a single-pass tokenizer handling '...' strings ('' doubled-quote + backslash escapes), "..." and `...` identifiers, line + block comments; semicolons and comment markers inside quotes are preserved verbatim. 7-case table test.

[x] Remove Postgres.Close(). Done 2026-06-10: deleted (it closed the caller's *sql.DB, which the migrator does not own); verified zero callers in openrails/doujins/authkit; ClickHouse.Close() retained — it closes only the lazily-opened native conn the migrator created. README notes the removal (minor-version bump on next tag).

[x] Document ClickHouse partial-apply semantics. Done 2026-06-10: README 'ClickHouse Semantics' section — no transactional DDL, failed multi-statement migration leaves earlier statements applied + migration unrecorded, every statement must be individually idempotent.

[x] Verify. Done 2026-06-10: go vet + go test ./... green (13 tests incl. sqlmock suites). Live tests (gated on MIGRATEKIT_TEST_DATABASE_URL, pgx stdlib added as test dep): TestPostgres_ConcurrentApply races 8 replica pools applying a non-idempotent migration (exactly-once asserted), TestPostgres_LockUnlockPinned (double-lock/unlock guards + cancelled-ctx release), TestPostgres_LockSurvivesPoolInterleaving reproduces the shared-pool production failure mode (50 lock/unlock cycles under pool churn). Revert-verified: restoring the old pool-based Lock/Unlock makes the suite fail.
=== OPTIONAL / DEFERRED ===
[x] (Optional) ClickHouse submodule split — DEFERRED 2026-06-10: no consumer has complained about go.sum weight; revisit only if one does. Recorded as a decision, no code change.

issues.name: v1.0.0 API freeze: define and document the stable API boundary
issues.description:
Pre-1.0 API review (2026-06-10). Decision inputs: a usage inventory across all consumers (openrails, doujins, authkit) showing what is actually called — LoadFromFS, NewPostgres/WithSchema, ApplyMigrations, Applied, Prefix, Migration, MigrationSource, ClickHouseConfig/NewClickHouse, ValidatePostgresMigrations, ValidateClickHouseMigrations — and zero callers of Apply/Lock/Unlock/Setup/Close.

DESIGN PRINCIPLE: freeze the smallest surface that covers real usage; everything dangerous-to-freeze and unused gets unexported now, while breaking is still free.

CHANGES MADE BEFORE THE FREEZE:
- Unexported Postgres.Apply / ClickHouse.Apply (single-apply bypassed the applied-set check — double-applies if misused) and Lock/Unlock on both (stateful pinned-connection locking should not be caller-driven). ApplyMigrations is the one supported path; ClickHouse.ApplyMigrations also now joins unlock errors like Postgres.
- Generalized MigrationSource.FS and the ValidateClickHouseMigrations filesystem parameter from embed.FS to fs.FS (source-compatible; embed.FS satisfies fs.FS).
- Kept public: Migration, Prefix, LoadFromFS, MigrationSource, ValidatePostgresMigrations, ValidateClickHouseMigrations, NewPostgres, WithSchema, Setup, Applied, ApplyMigrations, ValidateAllApplied, ClickHouseConfig, NewClickHouse, ClickHouse.{Setup,Applied,ApplyMigrations,ValidateAllApplied,Close}.

The README 'Stable API (v1)' section is the canonical boundary: full symbol tables with one-line contracts, 8 frozen behavioral contracts (tracking table shape, prefix tracking key, .up.sql discovery + numeric ordering + duplicate rejection, pinned advisory-lock serialization, template substitution rules, Postgres per-migration transactions, ClickHouse per-statement idempotency requirement, no ownership of caller's *sql.DB), a 'Removed in v1.0' list, and the compatibility policy (additive-only in v1.x; error TEXT not part of the API; v2 = new import path, very high bar).

[x] Generalize embed.FS -> fs.FS in MigrationSource.FS and ValidateClickHouseMigrations (source-compatible). Done 2026-06-10.

[x] Verify: go build/vet/test green incl. live lock tests. Done 2026-06-10.
